summary: Comments on Chuck Holland's proposed Remote Job Entry protocol in RFC 360. The author calls it an excellent document, then offers suggestions and small corrections, such as preferring the command QUIT to BYE and fixing the pathname syntax so host, socket and file names are used consistently across protocols.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 368 reviews a proposed protocol for submitting jobs to remote computers. It suggests changes to commands, file and host syntax, error messages and progress reporting.

subtitle: Suggestions for improving a proposed Remote Job Entry protocol

tldr.problem: A draft Remote Job Entry protocol needed review of its commands, syntax and handling of transfer progress.
tldr.mechanism: R. T. Braden comments on command names, pathname syntax, character codes, error messages and a transmission-status command.
tldr.outcome: The RFC records suggestions for refining the draft; it does not state which suggestions were adopted.

today: RFC 368 is a set of comments on a proposed RJE protocol. It records suggested improvements and does not say which ones became part of a later protocol.

sections.title: Reviewing the RJE Proposal
sections.content: R. T. Braden responds to Chuck Holland's proposed Remote Job Entry protocol in RFC 360. He calls the draft complete and consistent, then offers suggestions intended to improve the definition before wider use.
sections.plainLanguage: Braden reviewed a draft for sending jobs to remote computers. He praised the draft and listed changes he thought would make it clearer and more consistent.

sections.title: Commands, Names and Character Codes
sections.content:
Braden prefers QUIT to BYE and asks for a more consistent way to identify hosts, sockets and file names across network programs. He questions a PORT form tied to TIP conventions and suggests allowing hexadecimal and octal socket numbers, more transmission attributes and broader support for character codes.

He also recommends that syntax errors identify the specific invalid value, such as an unrecognized host name.
sections.plainLanguage: The suggestions call for clearer command names, consistent ways to write addresses and file names, support for more character codes, and error messages that name the problem.

sections.title: Showing Transfer Progress
sections.content: Based on experience submitting remote jobs to CCN, Braden says users want a command that reports how many records have been sent or received. He notes that network transfers can take a noticeable amount of time and that typical job output described in the RFC was about 30 pages.
sections.plainLanguage: Users wanted to check how much of a job had transferred while they waited. Braden suggests adding a command to show that progress.
